{{Short description|English physicist and mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Henry Cabourn Pocklington''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (28 January 1870, [[Exeter]] – 15 May 1952, [[Leeds]]) was an [[United Kingdom|English]] [[physicist]] and [[mathematician]]. His primary profession was as a [[schoolmaster]], but he made important contributions to [[number theory]] with the discovery of [[Pocklington primality test|Pocklington's primality test]] in 1914<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://services.spd.dcu.ie/johnbcos/download/3rd_year/Pocklington_1914/1914_PAP1.html |title=Pocklington's test |access-date=2007-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070207005132/http://services.spd.dcu.ie/johnbcos/download/3rd_year/Pocklington_1914/1914_PAP1.html |archive-date=2007-02-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the invention of [[Pocklington's algorithm]].  He also derived the first equation for the current in a wire [[antenna (radio)|antenna]], Pocklington's integral equation.<ref name="Pocklington">{{cite journal
